query: What professions did S. Sylvan Simon and Danny Cannon have in common?

pipeline_result.response:
S. Sylvan Simon and Danny Cannon both had the profession of being **film and television writers, directors, and producers**. They were both prominent figures in the entertainment industry during their respective eras.

- **S. Sylvan Simon** was primarily known as a director and producer, having worked on various films and television shows like "All That", "Wild Out", and "Stages".
- **Danny Cannon** was mainly recognized for his work as a rapper, actor, comedian, and producer. His career spanned from writing songs to producing films and television shows such as "The Nick Cannon Show", "Wild 'N Out", and "America's Got Talent".

Both artists contributed significantly to their respective fields in the entertainment industry.
retrieved_context: S. Sylvan Simon: S. Sylvan Simon (March 9, 1910 – May 17, 1951) was an American stage/film director and producer.
Danny Cannon: John Danny Cannon (born 1968 in Luton, England) is a British film and television writer, director and producer.

Nick Cannon: Nicholas Scott "Nick" Cannon (born October 8, 1980) is an American rapper, actor, comedian, director, screenwriter, film producer, entrepreneur, record producer, radio and television personality.  On television, Cannon began as a teenager on "All That" before going on to host "The Nick Cannon Show", "Wild 'N Out", and "America's Got Talent".  He acted in the films "Drumline", "Love Don't Cost a Thing", and "Roll Bounce".  As a rapper he released his debut self-titled album in 2003 with the hit single "Gigolo", a collaboration with singer R. Kelly.  In 2007 he played the role of the fictional footballer TJ Harper in the film "".  In 2006, Cannon recorded the singles "Dime Piece" and "My Wife" for the planned album "Stages", which was never released.  Cannon married American R&B/pop singer, Mariah Carey in 2008.  He filed for divorce in December 2014, after six years of marriage.  The divorce was finalized in 2016.
